title: Circular Dependency, Bean Scopes & Lazy Initialization in Spring (Hinglish) | CodeOrCap
description:
Spring Framework series (Hinglish): Circular Dependency, why constructor injection fails, how field/setter injection resolves it, why you should refactor instead, Singleton vs Prototype bean scopes, Eager vs Lazy initialization and @Lazy proxies. Includes 2 pause-and-think quizzes.

🔔 Subscribe to CodeOrCap for evidence-based tech content.

#Spring #SpringFramework #Java #CircularDependency #BeanScope #CodeOrCap

scenes.text: Welcome back Coder Army! Spring Framework series mein aaj teen bade topics: Circular Dependency, Bean Scopes, aur Bean Initialization.
Ye teeno topics aapas mein linked hain, aur inhe samajhne mein aapko bahut maza aayega.
Isse aapka Spring ka core knowledge aur strong hoga, aur interview mein ye sawaal bahut poochhe jaate hain. Chalo shuru karte hain!
Pehle ek quick recap. OrderService ko order place karne ke liye PaymentService ka object chahiye.
Yaani OrderService, PaymentService par dependent hai. Jab tak PaymentService ka object nahi, OrderService nahi ban sakti.
PaymentService ko khud ek PaymentGateway chahiye. To dependency ki ek poori chain ban jaati hai.
Spring ka IoC container bahut smart hai. Use pata hai ki pehle Gateway banana hai, phir Payment, aur sabse last mein Order.
Aur dependency inject bhi wahi karta hai. Seedhi line, koi dikkat nahi. Ab sochiye, agar ye line seedhi na ho to?
Maan lo do classes hain, A aur B. A ko banane ke liye B chahiye.
Aur B ko banane ke liye A chahiye. Yahi hai Circular Dependency.
Ab Spring ko samajh hi nahi aayega ki shuruaat kahan se kare. Pehle A banaye ya pehle B?
Apne example mein A ko OrderService maan lo, aur B ko PaymentService. Dono ek doosre par dependent hain.
Chalo code mein ise banate hain, aur dekhte hain ki Spring ise kaise handle karta hai.
IntelliJ mein ek naya Maven project banate hain, naam circular-dependency-demo.
Spring Core ke features chahiye, to pom mein spring-context ki dependency add karte hain. Version 7.0.7, kyunki hum Spring Boot 4 ke saath kaam karna chahte hain.
Maven reload karo, aur saari transitive dependencies bhi aa jaati hain.
Ab Main class mein IoC container start karte hain, AnnotationConfigApplicationContext ke saath.
AppConfig par Configuration aur ComponentScan lagao, taaki Spring har Component class ko scan kar sake.
Ek interesting baat: Configuration annotation ke andar bhi Component laga hota hai. Yaani AppConfig khud bhi ek bean hai.
Isi wajah se Spring AppConfig ke Bean methods ko call kar paata hai. Uska object container ke paas hota hai.
Pehle ek normal, bina circle wala version banate hain. OrderService par Component lagao.
Single constructor hai, to Autowired likhne ki zarurat nahi. Spring khud inject kar deta hai.
PaymentService mein bas ek pay method hai, jo print karta hai Payment done.
Main se getBean karke placeOrder call karte hain. Output: Payment done, phir Order placed. Sab sahi chal raha hai.
Ab zabardasti circular dependency banate hain. PaymentService ko bhi OrderService chahiye.
Aur pay method ke baad, ye OrderService ka getOrderDetails method call karti hai.
OrderService mein ye method bas Order details print karta hai.
Flow aisa hoga: placeOrder pay ko call karega, pay Payment done print karke getOrderDetails ko, aur last mein Order placed.
Lekin sabse pehla sawaal: kya Spring dono beans bana bhi payega?
Jawab hai nahi. OrderService ka constructor PaymentService maangta hai, aur PaymentService ka constructor OrderService.
Chalo run karke dekhte hain, kaunsa error milta hai.
Exception aa gayi: BeanCurrentlyInCreationException. Message: Requested bean is currently in creation. Is there an unresolvable circular reference?

Is there an unresolvable circular reference?

scenes.text: Matlab Spring ne OrderService banana shuru kiya, beech mein PaymentService banane gaya, aur PaymentService ne wapas OrderService maang li, jo abhi bana hi nahi.
Spring ko pata chal jaata hai ki bean pehle se creation state mein hai, aur wo exception throw kar deta hai.
Ek zaroori baat: ye problem Spring ki wajah se nahi aati. Ye aapke code design ki problem hai. Pure Java mein bhi ban sakti hai.
Do plain classes lo, A aur B, bina kisi Component ke. A ka constructor B maangta hai.
Aur B ka constructor A maangta hai. Ab main mein new A ke liye new B chahiye, aur new B ke liye new A.
Ek hack hai: default constructor mein A, B ko new karta hai, aur B, A ko new karta hai.
Ab new A chalao. A ka constructor B banata hai, B ka constructor wapas A banata hai, aur ye chakkar chalta rahta hai.
Stack memory bhar jaati hai, aur aakhir mein StackOverflowError aa jaata hai. Yaani pure Java mein bhi ye bug ban sakta hai.
Wapas Spring par aate hain. Error constructor injection ki wajah se aa rahi thi, kyunki dono ek doosre ka object constructor mein maangte the.
Ek tareeka hai ki constructor injection hata kar field injection ya setter injection par chale jao.
Dono classes se constructor hata do, aur field par Autowired laga do.
PaymentService mein bhi bilkul yahi. Setter injection mein bhi kahani wahi rehti, bas setter method par Autowired lagta.
Ek interesting sawaal: field to private hai. Spring bina setter ya constructor ke usme object kaise daal deta hai?
Jawab: Java Reflection. Spring ke paas poori class ka access hota hai, aur Reflection API se wo private members mein bhi values inject kar deta hai.
Ab main run karo. Payment done, Order details, Order placed. Spring ne circular dependency solve kar di!
Lekin ye hua kaise? Yahi samajhna sabse zaroori hai.
Field ya setter injection mein object banana aur dependency inject karna, dono alag ho jaate hain.
Constructor injection kehta hai: mujhe banane ke liye hi meri dependency chahiye. Field injection kehta hai: pehle mujhe khali bana do, dependency baad mein daal dena.
Spring ka normal flow: pehle A create, phir A ki dependency inject. Uske baad B create, phir B ki dependency inject.
Ab circular case mein Spring OrderService ka partial object bana leta hai. Constructor chal gaya, lekin dependency abhi inject nahi hui.
Phir wo dependency resolve karne jaata hai. PaymentService chahiye. Container mein check karta hai, nahi hai, to PaymentService ka khali object bana deta hai.
Ab PaymentService ko OrderService chahiye. Container mein dekhta hai, partial hi sahi, wo maujood hai. Wahi inject kar deta hai.
Phir wapas OrderService mein PaymentService inject hoti hai. Dono ek doosre ko sahi point karte hain, aur dono complete ho jaate hain.
Isi concept ko kehte hain early reference. Object poora bana nahi, lekin uska reference pehle de diya jaata hai.
Lekin ye constructor injection mein nahi ho sakta, kyunki wahan object banta hi dependency milne ke baad hai.
To problem solve ho gayi? Technically haan, lekin practically ye achhi coding practice nahi hai.
Spring Boot 2.6 ke baad circular references by default disallow hain. Property hai spring dot main dot allow-circular-references, aur uski default value false hai.
Yaani Spring Boot mein ye code aisa hi chalega nahi. Chahe field injection ho ya setter injection, wo dono ko error dega, jab tak aap property true na karo.
Plain Spring Core mein ye supported hai, lekin enterprise applications mein circular dependency honi hi nahi chahiye.
Wajah? Aisa code tightly coupled hota hai. Do classes ek doosre ke bina kaam hi nahi kar sakti.
Aur sochiye, aisa hota hi kyun hai? Iska matlab hamne responsibilities ko sahi se alag nahi kiya. Single Responsibility Principle toot gaya.
Quick quiz: circular dependency ka sabse achha solution kya hai? Rukkar socho. Jawab: design refactor karo.

quiz.question: Best fix for a circular dependency?

scenes.text: To fix kaise karein? Dekhte hain ki circular dependency aa kyun rahi hai. Wajah hai getOrderDetails ka PaymentService se call hona.
OrderService ka kaam hai orders handle karna. Usne payment ka kaam PaymentService ko delegate kar diya, ye theek hai.
Lekin payment ho jaane ke baad PaymentService order ke details kyun maange? Ye uska kaam hai hi nahi. Uska kaam hai sirf payment handle karna.
To ye call PaymentService se hata do, aur OrderService ke andar le aao. Payment hone ke baad OrderService khud details print karegi.
Ab PaymentService ko OrderService ki zarurat hi nahi. Field aur constructor dono hata sakte ho.
Dependency ab ek taraf ki hai. OrderService, PaymentService par depend karti hai, lekin wapas nahi. Circular dependency khatam.
Output bilkul same: Payment done, Order details, Order placed. Lekin code ab clean aur design sahi hai.
Yaad rakhna: circular dependency ko solve mat karo, use hata do. Ye enterprise level ka sabse bada rule hai.
Ab agla topic: Bean Scopes. Ek naye project mein samjhte hain, bean-scope-demo.
Ek khali OrderService bana lo, Component laga hua, aur uske constructor mein print karo Order service created.
Main mein getBean se ek baar OrderService maango, aur doosre variable order2 mein dobara maango.
Sawaal: kya do object bane honge, ya dono ko ek hi object ka reference mila? Rukkar socho.
Run karo. Order service created sirf ek baar print hua, aur double equals ka jawab true. Yaani ek hi object tha.
Container ne ek hi object banaya, aur har baar wahi reference wapas kiya. Ise kehte hain Singleton scope.
Java mein mainly do scopes hote hain: Singleton aur Prototype. Baaki scopes web application mein kaam aate hain.
Singleton kehta hai: ek bean definition ke liye ek hi object banega. Kitni baar bhi getBean karo, wahi object milega.
Ye default scope hai. Aap likh bhi sakte ho, Scope annotation mein singleton, tab bhi kuch nahi badlega.
Ab Prototype ko dekhte hain. Ye bilkul ulta hai: jab bhi aap object maangoge, har baar naya object milega.
Wahi Main chalao. Ab Order service created do baar print hota hai, aur double equals ka jawab false.
Chahe getBean se maango, ya dependency injection ke liye, har baar ek naya object banega. Ye bilkul new keyword jaisa hai.
Maan lo do aur classes A aur B, dono OrderService ko constructor mein maangti hain. Singleton mein dono ko ek hi object milega.
Prototype mein A ko alag object milega, B ko alag. Aur Main ke do getBean ke do aur. Total chaar objects.
Ab ek bahut hi important point, jisme log confuse ho jaate hain. Spring ka singleton, Singleton design pattern jaisa nahi hai.
Design pattern kehta hai ki ek Java class ka sirf ek hi object ban sakta hai. Bahut strict.
Spring mein singleton ka matlab sirf itna hai: ek bean definition ke liye ek object.
Aap khud new keyword se jitne chaho objects bana sakte ho. Spring unhe manage nahi karega.

scenes.text: Aur agar AppConfig mein Bean ke saath do methods likho jo OrderService return karte hain, to do alag bean definitions ho jaati hain.
Run karo to Order service created do baar print hota hai. Container mein ab OrderService ke do beans hain, aur har ek khud mein singleton hai.
Lekin ab agar koi OrderService inject karwaye, to Spring confuse ho jaayega ki kaunsa dena hai, aur NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException aayegi.
Iska solution hum Primary aur Qualifier se pehle dekh chuke hain. Bas yaad rakhna: scope bean definition ke hisaab se kaam karta hai.
Ab practical sawaal: kab singleton, aur kab prototype? Ek User class socho, jisme name aur age fields hain.
Ye saari properties us object ki state hain. Har user ka naam aur age alag hogi.
Agar User singleton hua, to container ke paas bas ek user hoga, jiska naam Aditya aur age 28. Har getBean par wahi milega.
Hum chahte hain ki application mein multiple users hon. To jis class mein state hai, use hamesha prototype banao.
Aur singleton ke liye class stateless honi chahiye, yaani apni koi state na rakhe.
Iske best candidates hain service aur manager classes: OrderService, PaymentService, OrderManager. Wo bahut orders handle karti hain, lekin khud ki koi state nahi rakhti.
Aur request, session, application jaise scopes bhi hote hain. Wo web application mein kaam aate hain, jo hum Spring MVC mein padhenge.
Quiz time: UserSession class, jisme har user ka data hai, kaunsa scope hona chahiye? Socho. Jawab: prototype, ya web scope.
Ab teesra topic: Bean Initialization. Beans do tarah se initialize ho sakte hain, Eager aur Lazy.
Eager ka matlab: jaise hi application context start hua, saare beans turant create ho jaate hain.
Demo ke liye do classes lo, OrderService aur PaymentService, dono Component, aur constructors mein print. Main mein kuch bhi call nahi.
Run karte hi screen par aata hai: Order service created, Payment service created. Container start hote hi dono bean ban gaye.
Ye default hai. Singleton scope ke beans by default eager hote hain.
Agar aap chaho to ek heavy class ko Lazy bana sakte ho. Class par Lazy annotation lagao.
Dono par Lazy lagao aur run karo. Ab kuch bhi print nahi hota. Container start hua, lekin koi object nahi bana.
Jab aap context getBean se OrderService maangoge, tabhi uska object banega, aur tabhi print hoga.
Ab baat prototype ki. Prototype par Lazy likhne ki zarurat hi nahi. Wo hamesha lazy hi hota hai.
Kyunki prototype kehta hai, jab bhi maangoge naya object doonga. To pehle se ek object bana kar rakhne ka fayda hi kya?
Aur singleton mein ye hota hai: sabko wahi ek object dena hai, to pehle hi bana ke rakh lo. Isliye singleton eager hota hai.
Yaani Lazy sirf singleton ko lazy banata hai. Prototype ko eager banane ka koi tareeka hi nahi.
Ek property bhi hai: spring dot main dot lazy-initialization. True kar do to saare beans globally lazy ho jaate hain.
Phir koi ek class eager chahiye to uspar Lazy ke saath value false likh do. Baaki sab lazy rahenge.
To Spring eager ko prefer kyun karta hai? Kyunki fail fast. Wiring ki saari galtiyan application start hote hi pakdi jaati hain.
Agar lazy hua, to ho sakta hai production par jab pehli baar bean maanga jaaye, tab application phat jaaye. Isliye heavy classes ke liye hi Lazy use karo.
Ab dekhte hain Lazy ka ek aur interesting use. Wapas constructor wali circular dependency par chalte hain.
Ab maan lo PaymentService par Lazy lagaya, aur constructor se circular dependency hai. Spring OrderService banayega, lekin PaymentService nahi.
Phir bhi OrderService ko PaymentService chahiye. To Spring ek proxy object inject kar deta hai.
Proxy ek design pattern hai: ek fake object jo PaymentService jaisa dikhta hai, lekin asli PaymentService nahi hota.
Isi tarah aap constructor ke parameter par bhi Lazy laga sakte ho. Ye aksar circular dependency todne ke liye use hota hai.
Jab tak placeOrder call nahi hota, proxy hi rehta hai. Jaise hi payment dot pay chalta hai, asli PaymentService banta hai.
Us waqt PaymentService ko OrderService chahiye, wo already ban chuki hai. Dono sahi wire ho jaate hain, aur proxy hat jaata hai.
Ye bhi circular dependency solve karne ka ek tareeka hai. Lekin phir wahi baat: solve nahi, refactor karna hi sahi hai.
Aur ek aur tareeka aage Bean Lifecycle mein aayega, PostConstruct annotation ke saath. Lekin wo bhi sirf workaround hai.
Recap: circular dependency tab aati hai jab do beans ek doosre par depend karein. Constructor injection mein ye fail ho jaati hai.

items: Circular = A needs B, B needs A

scenes.text: Singleton mein ek bean definition ka ek object banta hai, aur prototype mein har baar naya. Stateless ko singleton, stateful ko prototype banao.
Singleton eager hota hai, lekin Lazy se lazy ho sakta hai. Prototype hamesha lazy hota hai. Fail fast ke liye eager hi behtar.
Ab ek practice: kuch classes par Lazy, kuch par singleton aur prototype lagao, aur khud socho ki output kya aayega. Fir run karke check karo.
Agle video mein Bean Lifecycle dekhenge. Video pasand aaya to like karo, aur CodeOrCap ko subscribe karna mat bhoolna.
